mission: Arrive at your second shot with a clear view of the green. Favor attackable position over maximum distance. No hero recoveries.

holes.plan: Stock driver leaves roughly 120. Commit to the corridor, then PW territory.
holes.advice: Driver here. Favor the left half; the right fairway bunker is the trouble to avoid. A solid drive leaves around a PW.

holes.plan: Three-shot hole by default. Advance safely and build the third shot around 80â€“100 yards.
holes.danger: Do not force the second shot.
holes.advice: Let’s play this in three. Driver toward center-left, then advance safely to leave an 80–100 yard third. There’s no need to force the second.

holes.plan: Position first. Expect roughly 8iâ€“9i and favor middle green.
holes.danger: Avoid turning a hard hole into a recovery hole.
holes.advice: This is one of the tougher holes. Driver toward the center, just a little right. You’ll have roughly an 8i or 9i; take the middle of the green.

holes.plan: Good drive creates a short wedge approach.
holes.advice: Driver toward the left-center. Keep the right-side bunkers out of the picture and a good drive gives you a short wedge.

holes.plan: Stock PW. Green first, pin second.
holes.advice: Stock PW. Favor the middle or right-center of the green, away from the left bunker. Get on the green before thinking about the pin.

holes.plan: 3H leaves roughly 70 yards and keeps the hole simple.
holes.danger: Driver brings left water near green into play.
holes.advice: 3H is plenty here. Aim center-right and leave about 70 yards. Driver brings the water left of the green into play; we don’t need it.

holes.plan: Default layup after drive; build a comfortable wedge third.
holes.danger: Attack in two only from a perfect lie and lane.
holes.advice: Driver toward center-right, then plan on a layup to a comfortable wedge. Only think about going in two if the lie and line are both perfect.
4i toward the left-center of the green. The right bunker is the one to avoid; the middle of the green is a good result.

holes.danger: Left bunker around driver corridor; right green bunkering.
holes.advice: Driver toward center-right to stay away from the left fairway bunker. A good one leaves about a 9i. Remember the bunkers right of the green on the approach.

holes.plan: Commit through staggered fairway bunkers; wedge approach.
holes.danger: Do not steer the tee ball.
holes.advice: Driver down the center. Choose your line through the staggered fairway bunkers and commit. A good drive leaves a wedge.

holes.plan: Play for position, then middle green. Bogey is acceptable.
holes.advice: This is the toughest hole today. Driver toward left-center, then middle of the green. Five is fine; don’t chase four after a bad shot.

holes.plan: Driver clears long left bunker; expect around 7i.
holes.advice: Driver toward right-center. The plan is to get past the long left bunker and leave around a 7i. Keep yourself a clear approach.

holes.plan: Stock PW and take the middle.
holes.advice: Stock PW toward center-right. Stay away from the left bunker and take the middle of the green.

holes.plan: Intentional three-shot plan. Lay up to a preferred wedge number.
holes.danger: Do not let reachable-looking yardage force aggression.
holes.advice: Play this in three. Driver down the center, then lay up to your preferred wedge distance. Don’t let the yardage talk you into forcing the second.

holes.plan: Slight uphill. Smooth 5i if conditions make 6i marginal.
holes.advice: 6i toward center-right, away from the left bunker. It plays a little uphill; take a smooth 5i if the conditions make 6i a stretch.

holes.danger: Driver creates awkward pitch / greenside bunker risk.
holes.advice: 3H down the center leaves about 75–80 yards, close to your stock 60°. Driver risks an awkward pitch or the greenside bunker. Keep this one simple.

holes.plan: Uphill. Good drive leaves PW/9i range.
holes.advice: Driver toward center-left. This one is uphill; a good drive leaves PW or 9i range. Keep the right greenside bunker in mind on the approach.

holes.plan: Good drive may leave ~175. Attack only with clean lie; otherwise wedge setup.
holes.danger: 3H can fall into staggered bunker corridor.
holes.advice: Driver toward center-left. A good one may leave around 175 yards. Go for it only from a clean lie with a clear line; otherwise set up a wedge. 3H can finish among the staggered bunkers.

gamePlan: Driver when there is room for your normal shot. Choose 3H when driver brings trouble into play. Leave yourself a comfortable next shot.
Favor the middle of the green. On the par 5s, build a comfortable wedge approach unless the lie and line make going for it a clear choice.
Get back into position. Take the simple recovery and keep one bad shot from becoming two.
A clear view of the green matters more than a few extra yards. Choose your target and commit.
